C05-M01-L01-F1.title: The seven PTES phases as one engagement
C05-M01-L01-F1.caption: PTES runs from pre-engagement to reporting, with lessons and retests feeding the next engagement.
C05-M01-L01-F1.alt: Top-to-bottom graph of seven phases: Pre-engagement interactions (scope, RoE, authorisation), Intelligence gathering (assets, technologies, people), Threat modelling (business assets and threat communities), Vulnerability analysis (discover and validate weaknesses), Exploitation (minimum proof that a weakness is real), Post-exploitation (value of access, record every change) and Reporting (executive summary + technical findings). A dashed loop arrow from Reporting back to Pre-engagement interactions is labelled: lessons and retest feed the next engagement.

nodes.label: Exploitation
nodes.sub: minimum proof that a weakness is real

nodes.label: Post-exploitation
nodes.sub: value of access, record every change

edges.label: lessons and retest feed the next engagement

C05-M01-L01-F1.note: Agree first, analyse before you attack, prove rather than exploit, and treat the report as the product.

C05-M01-L01-F2.title: OSSTMM 3 test scope: the five channels
C05-M01-L01-F2.caption: The OSSTMM test scope decomposes into five channels, each of which must be stated as tested or not tested.
C05-M01-L01-F2.alt: Tree diagram. Root: OSSTMM 3 test scope, measure porosity against controls. Five children: Human (PHYSSEC: people and procedures), Physical (PHYSSEC: sites, hardware, perimeters), Wireless (SPECSEC: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID), Telecommunications (COMSEC: telephony networks) and Data networks (COMSEC: wired networks and hosts), the last highlighted as the channel the course lab exercises.
C05-M01-L01-F2.note: Every report states which channels were tested and which were not.
